rules.purpose: Detect a local variable read at a return sink on a feasible control-flow path where no reaching assignment exists.
preconditions: A Python function is fully available within the pinned declared scope.
The target name is a function-local variable and the relevant return is syntactically resolved.
The task contract explicitly defines the behavior for the branch or path under examination.
sufficient_evidence: A bounded control-flow analysis identifies a feasible path to the return where the target local has no reaching definition.
The task contract requires a return value on that path, and no parameter, prior assignment, exception binding, or supported closure binding defines the name.
counterevidence: A reaching assignment exists on every feasible path to the return.
The name is a parameter, global, nonlocal, closure binding, or valid exception target under supported semantics.
The path is infeasible under a proven condition.
abstain_when: Control flow requires unsupported dynamic semantics, eval or exec, reflective mutation, or unresolved imports.
Path feasibility cannot be established within the declared analysis budget.
The task contract does not specify the required behavior for the path.

rules.purpose: Detect a caught exception that is returned as a fallback when the declared contract requires the exception to propagate.
preconditions: The function and handler are fully available in the pinned declared scope.
A structured task-visible contract specifies the exception type and required propagation behavior.
The call that can raise the specified exception is inside the analyzed handler.
sufficient_evidence: The handler catches the specified exception or a proven superclass.
The handler returns or otherwise completes normally without re-raising the exception.
The contract requires propagation to the caller.
counterevidence: The handler re-raises the caught exception or raises a contractually equivalent exception.
The contract explicitly permits the fallback behavior.
The caught exception cannot originate from the contract-relevant operation.
abstain_when: The exception type relationship cannot be resolved.
The handler or relevant call is outside the pinned scope.
The contract does not specify propagation semantics.

rules.purpose: Determine whether a contract-relevant intermediate value reaches the declared output sink or is bypassed by a stale input value.
preconditions: The task-visible contract supplies a structured formula or input and output examples sufficient for bounded checking.
The relevant function body and output sink are fully available.
The supported expression subset can be interpreted without executing repository code.
sufficient_evidence: A definition-to-sink data-flow trace shows the contract-relevant intermediate is not consumed by the output expression.
A bounded, side-effect-free interpretation of the declared input case yields a value inconsistent with the task-visible expected result.
The mismatch is attributable to the stale value path, not unsupported coercion or environment behavior.
counterevidence: The intermediate reaches the output sink through a supported alias or helper.
The output expression satisfies the declared contract for all enumerated cases.
A supported conversion or later operation makes the apparent stale value equivalent.
abstain_when: The contract is only implicit natural language and cannot be normalized unambiguously.
The expression uses unsupported calls, mutation, descriptors, dynamic dispatch, or external state.
The enumerated input and output evidence does not isolate the suspected data-flow cause.

rules.purpose: Establish that a target local is initialized on every supported path to its use and that enumerated task-visible cases satisfy the declared function contract.
preconditions: The complete function body and task-visible input and output examples are available.
All branches and expressions are within the registered static analysis subset.
The decision is explicitly scoped to the named property and enumerated contract cases.
sufficient_evidence: Every feasible path to the target use has a reaching assignment.
A bounded pure-expression interpreter evaluates every declared input case to its expected result.
No relevant unsupported path or side effect is omitted.
counterevidence: Any feasible path reaches the use without assignment.
Any declared contract case produces a different value or exception behavior.
A relevant branch or dependency is outside the analyzed scope.
abstain_when: The function uses unsupported dynamic features or external state.
The task-visible contract does not enumerate the behavior needed for the scoped decision.

rules.purpose: Preserve a visible attribute mismatch as an observation while abstaining when dynamic provider construction prevents a closed-world contract conclusion.
preconditions: The consumer attribute read and visible provider declarations are available.
The task-visible evidence explicitly identifies an unresolved dynamic provider, wrapper, inheritance, or factory boundary.
sufficient_evidence: The requested attribute is not declared in the visible provider class, while a related but differently named attribute is declared.
The provider construction or import path is unresolved or its implementation is outside the pinned evidence scope.
No explicit closed-world interface contract proves the attribute is forbidden.
counterevidence: The provider or a resolved base class declares the requested attribute.
A verified dynamic wrapper or runtime contract supplies the attribute.
A complete interface schema explicitly defines the requested attribute.
abstain_when: The dynamic provider implementation or runtime construction path is absent.
The evidence cannot distinguish a typo from supported dynamic attribute provision.
